#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Claude Code Stop hook: run the test suite when Claude finishes a turn that
# changed code (src/, tests/, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock).
#
# Skipping:
#   - Slow tests carry #[ignore = "slow"]; plain `cargo test` (what this hook
#     runs) skips them. Run them with `cargo test -- --include-ignored`.
#   - MUSICRS_SKIP_HOOK_TESTS=1 in the environment Claude Code was started
#     from disables the hook entirely.
#
# Exit 2 with the failure output on stderr makes Claude keep working on it.
set -uo pipefail

input=$(cat)
[[ "${MUSICRS_SKIP_HOOK_TESTS:-0}" == "1" ]] && exit 0

cd "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(dirname "$0")/../..}" || exit 0

stamp_dir=target/.claude-hook
mkdir -p "$stamp_dir"
paths=(src tests Cargo.toml Cargo.lock)

# Cheap fingerprint of the code: name, size and mtime of every tracked or
# untracked (non-ignored) file under the code paths.
fingerprint=$(git ls-files -co --exclude-standard -- "${paths[@]}" \
  | xargs -r -d '\n' stat -c '%n %s %Y' 2>/dev/null | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)

# Nothing changed since the last passing run.
[[ -f "$stamp_dir/passed" && "$(cat "$stamp_dir/passed")" == "$fingerprint" ]] && exit 0

# First run on a clean tree: assume the committed code is tested.
if [[ ! -f "$stamp_dir/passed" && -z "$(git status --porcelain -- "${paths[@]}")" ]]; then
  echo "$fingerprint" > "$stamp_dir/passed"
  exit 0
fi

# Claude already saw these failures and stopped without changing code: let it
# stop instead of looping.
stop_hook_active=$(jq -r '.stop_hook_active // false' <<<"$input" 2>/dev/null)
if [[ "$stop_hook_active" == "true" && -f "$stamp_dir/failed" \
      && "$(cat "$stamp_dir/failed")" == "$fingerprint" ]]; then
  exit 0
fi

log="$stamp_dir/last-run.log"
if cargo test --quiet >"$log" 2>&1; then
  echo "$fingerprint" > "$stamp_dir/passed"
  rm -f "$stamp_dir/failed"
  exit 0
fi

echo "$fingerprint" > "$stamp_dir/failed"
{
  echo "Stop hook: \`cargo test\` failed (slow #[ignore] tests skipped). Fix the failures before finishing. Last 80 lines of $log:"
  tail -n 80 "$log"
} >&2
exit 2
name: CI

on:
  # Every pull request, whatever its base, so PRs stacked on another PR's branch get CI too
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read
  checks: write
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  test:
    name: Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy

      - name: Cache cargo registry & build artifacts
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2

      - name: Install cargo-nextest
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest

      - name: Check formatting
        run: cargo fmt --check

      - name: Clippy
        run: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings

      - name: Build
        run: cargo build --all-targets

      - name: Run tests (nextest + JUnit output)
        run: |
          cargo nextest run \
            --profile ci \
            --run-ignored all \
            --no-fail-fast \
            2>&1

      - name: Publish test results
        uses: EnricoMi/publish-unit-test-result-action@v2
        if: always()
        with:
          files: target/nextest/ci/junit.xml
          check_name: Test Results
          comment_mode: always
          fail_on: test failures

     3	//! Rust port of [pyMUSIC](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/pyMUSIC) — an implementation of the
     4	//! **MUSIC** (MUltiple SIgnal Classification) algorithm for Direction-of-Arrival (DOA) estimation
     5	//! with microphone/antenna arrays.
     6	//!
     7	//! ## Overview
     8	//!
     9	//! The MUSIC algorithm decomposes the covariance matrix of array observations into signal and
    10	//! noise subspaces. Steering vectors that are orthogonal to the noise subspace indicate the
    11	//! directions from which signals arrive. Peaks in the resulting pseudo-spectrum correspond to
    12	//! estimated arrival angles.
    13	//!
    14	//! ## Quick Start

     8	/// Computes the analytic signal of a real-valued input using the Hilbert transform.
     9	///
    10	/// The analytic signal `z(t) = x(t) + j·H{x(t)}` has a one-sided spectrum; its magnitude is the
    11	/// instantaneous envelope and its argument is the instantaneous phase.
    12	///
    13	/// # Algorithm
    14	/// 1. Forward FFT of the real input.
    15	/// 2. Apply the one-sided spectral window H: `H[0] = 1`, `H[k] = 2` for the positive
    16	///    frequencies `1 ≤ k < (N+1)/2`, `H[N/2] = 1` for the Nyquist bin of even N, and `H = 0` for
    17	///    the negative frequencies `k > N/2` (as in `scipy.signal.hilbert`).
    18	/// 3. Inverse FFT → analytic signal.
    19	///
    20	/// # Examples
    21	/// ```
    22	/// use musicrs::analytic_signal;
    23	/// use std::f64::consts::PI;
    24	/// let n = 256;
    25	/// let cos: Vec<f64> = (0..n).map(|i| (2.0 * PI * 10.0 * i as f64 / n as f64).cos()).collect();
    26	/// let z = analytic_signal(&cos);
    27	/// // Magnitude should be approximately 1 everywhere (after transients settle)
    28	/// for &c in &z[10..n-10] {
    29	///     assert!((c.norm() - 1.0).abs() < 0.01);
    30	/// }
    31	/// ```
    32	pub fn analytic_signal(data: &[f64]) -> Vec<Complex<f64>> {
    33	    let n = data.len();
    34	    if n == 0 {
    35	        return Vec::new();
    36	    }
    37	    let mut planner = FftPlanner::<f64>::new();
    38	
    39	    // Forward FFT
    40	    let fft_forward = planner.plan_fft_forward(n);
    41	    let mut spectrum: Vec<Complex<f64>> = data.iter().map(|&x| Complex::new(x, 0.0)).collect();
    42	    fft_forward.process(&mut spectrum);
    43	
    44	    // One-sided spectral window. DC is unchanged; so is the Nyquist bin N/2, which only
    45	    // exists for even N. Odd N has no Nyquist bin: bin (N-1)/2 is a positive frequency.
    46	    for sample in &mut spectrum[1..n.div_ceil(2)] {
    47	        *sample *= 2.0;
    48	    }
    49	    for sample in &mut spectrum[n / 2 + 1..] {
    50	        *sample = Complex::new(0.0, 0.0);
    51	    }
    52	
    53	    // Inverse FFT
    54	    let fft_inverse = planner.plan_fft_inverse(n);
    55	    fft_inverse.process(&mut spectrum);
    56	
    57	    // Normalise
    58	    let norm = n as f64;
    59	    spectrum.iter().map(|c| c / norm).collect()
    60	}

    96	///     assert_eq!(peak, 2);

   102	        return Err(MusicError::InvalidNfft);
   103	    }
   104	    if no_overlap >= nfft {

   111	    // Use real-to-complex FFT plan (standard forward FFT on real-padded input)
   112	    let fft = planner.plan_fft_forward(nfft);
   113	
   114	    let num_windows = if data.len() >= nfft {
   115	        (data.len() - nfft) / step + 1
   116	    } else {
   117	        0
   118	    };

   122	        vec![vec![Complex::new(0.0, 0.0); num_windows]; freq_bins];

   126	        let mut buf: Vec<Complex<f64>> = data[start..end]
   127	            .iter()
   128	            .map(|&x| Complex::new(x, 0.0))
   129	            .collect();

   131	        for bin in 0..freq_bins {

1	//! # musicrs
     2	//!
     3	//! Rust port of [pyMUSIC](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/pyMUSIC) — an implementation of the
     4	//! **MUSIC** (MUltiple SIgnal Classification) algorithm for Direction-of-Arrival (DOA) estimation
     5	//! with microphone/antenna arrays.
     6	//!
     7	//! ## Overview
     8	//!
     9	//! The MUSIC algorithm decomposes the covariance matrix of array observations into signal and
    10	//! noise subspaces. Steering vectors that are orthogonal to the noise subspace indicate the
    11	//! directions from which signals arrive. Peaks in the resulting pseudo-spectrum correspond to
    12	//! estimated arrival angles.
    13	//!
    14	//! ## Quick Start
    15	//!
    16	//! ```rust
    17	//! use musicrs::MusicEstimator;
    18	//! use nalgebra::DMatrix;
    19	//!
    20	//! // Default Kinect 4-mic linear array, 720 angle steps over [0, 2π), 16 kHz
    21	//! let estimator = MusicEstimator::default();
    22	//!
    23	//! // `real_data` is 4 × N real-valued microphone data (e.g. read from a WAV file).
    24	//! // Here: silence plus a tiny 300 Hz tone, just to show the call.
    25	//! let real_data = DMatrix::from_fn(4, 1600, |_, t| {
    26	//!     (2.0 * std::f64::consts::PI * 300.0 * t as f64 / 16000.0).cos()
    27	//! });
    28	//!
    29	//! // Analytic signal per channel, covariance, noise subspace, pseudo-spectrum, peaks:
    30	//! let angles = estimator.estimate_doa_from_real(&real_data, 1, 300.0)?;
    31	//! println!("DOA estimate: {:.1}°", angles[0].to_degrees());
    32	//! # Ok::<(), musicrs::MusicError>(())
    33	//! ```
    34	//!
    35	//! Use [`MusicEstimator::estimate_doa`] directly if you already have complex data, and
    36	//! [`MusicEstimator::ifb_music_spectrum`] for the wideband (IFB) variant.
    37	
    38	pub mod error;
    39	pub mod music;
    40	pub mod stft;
    41	
    42	pub use error::MusicError;
    43	pub use music::{MusicEstimator, select_bins_by_energy};
    44	pub use stft::{analytic_signal, stft};

     5	/// Why a musicrs function could not produce a result.
     6	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
     7	pub enum MusicError {
     8	    /// The data (or noise subspace) has the wrong number of rows: one per antenna is
     9	    /// expected.
    10	    RowCountMismatch { expected: usize, got: usize },
    11	    /// The covariance matrix is not `n_antennas × n_antennas`.
    12	    CovarianceShape {
    13	        n_antennas: usize,
    14	        rows: usize,
    15	        cols: usize,
    16	    },
    17	    /// The data has no rows or no samples.
    18	    EmptyData,
    19	    /// The data is shorter than one STFT window, so it has no complete window.
    20	    DataShorterThanWindow { nfft: usize, samples: usize },
    21	    /// The data contains a NaN or infinite value.
    22	    NonFiniteData,
    23	    /// The data (after removing each channel's mean, for real data) is all zeros, or
    24	    /// every selected frequency bin is: there is no signal to locate.
    25	    SilentData,
    26	    /// `n_sources` must be less than the number of antennas, so that a noise subspace
    27	    /// is left.
    28	    TooManySources { n_sources: usize, n_antennas: usize },
    29	    /// The STFT window size `nfft` is 0.
    30	    InvalidNfft,

//! MUSIC (MUltiple SIgnal Classification) algorithm for Direction-of-Arrival estimation.

use std::f64::consts::PI;

use nalgebra::DMatrix;
use nalgebra::DVector;
use num_complex::Complex;

use crate::error::{MusicError, Result};
use crate::stft::{analytic_signal, stft};

/// Speed of sound in air at ~20 °C, in metres per second.
const SPEED_OF_SOUND: f64 = 343.2;

/// Power ratio (−260 dB) below which a signal counts as silent: above the rounding residue
/// left by removing a constant offset or by FFT leakage from an on-bin tone (about
/// ε² ≈ 5e-32 times a small factor), but low enough that a quiet tone on a large DC
/// offset (say 1e-5 on 1e6, a ratio of 1e-22) still counts as signal.
const SILENCE_RATIO: f64 = 1e-26;

/// Default Kinect microphone array positions `(x, y)` in metres.
const DEFAULT_ANTENNA_POSITIONS: [[f64; 2]; 4] =
    [[0.113, 0.0], [-0.036, 0.0], [-0.076, 0.0], [-0.113, 0.0]];

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Type aliases
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
type Cplx = Complex<f64>;
type CMatrix = DMatrix<Cplx>;
type CVec = DVector<Cplx>;

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Hermitian eigendecomposition (pure nalgebra, no LAPACK)
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Eigendecomposition of a complex Hermitian n×n matrix using faer's dedicated
/// complex selfadjoint solver, which is numerically more stable than the real
/// block-matrix trick for near-degenerate noise subspaces.
///
/// Returns `(eigenvalues, eigenvectors)` sorted by ascending eigenvalue.
/// `eigenvalues[k]` is real; `eigenvectors.column(k)` is the unit-norm eigenvector.
fn hermitian_eigen(mat: &CMatrix) -> (Vec<f64>, CMatrix) {
    use faer::complex_native::c64;
    use faer::{Mat as FaerMat, Side};

    let n = mat.nrows();

    // Convert nalgebra complex matrix → faer complex matrix
    let faer_mat: FaerMat<c64> = FaerMat::from_fn(n, n, |i, j| {
        let c = mat[(i, j)];
        c64::new(c.re, c.im)
    });

    // Numerically stable Hermitian eigendecomposition
    // Note: faer does not guarantee a sort order, so we sort ascending afterward.
    let evd = faer_mat.selfadjoint_eigendecomposition(Side::Lower);

    // Eigenvalues are real but stored as c64 with im ≈ 0; extract via .re
    let s_col = evd.s().column_vector();
    let u_mat = evd.u();

    // Sort by ascending (real) eigenvalue
    let mut order: Vec<usize> = (0..n).collect();
    order.sort_unstable_by(|&a, &b| s_col.read(a).re.total_cmp(&s_col.read(b).re));

    let eigenvalues: Vec<f64> = order.iter().map(|&i| s_col.read(i).re).collect();
    // Copy the eigenvectors (reordered by ascending eigenvalue) back into nalgebra.
    // faer's eigenvectors already satisfy A·v = λ·v, so no conjugation is applied;
    // the steering-vector sign convention in `steering_vector` is matched to this.
    let eigenvectors: CMatrix = CMatrix::from_fn(n, n, |row, col| {
        let src_col = order[col];
        let c = u_mat.read(row, src_col);
        Cplx::new(c.re, c.im)
    });

    (eigenvalues, eigenvectors)
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Peak detection
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Returns the angles of the `n` highest peaks in `scores`, sorted by descending peak
/// height.
///
/// A peak is a run of one or more equal neighbouring scores that is strictly higher than
/// the scores on either side of it; it is reported at the run's midpoint. Runs of equal
/// scores happen on symmetric spectra: a line array's spectrum is mirror-symmetric, so a
/// source at endfire between two grid points scores exactly the same on both.
///
/// With `circular` (the grid covers the full circle), the first and last points are
/// neighbours and a run may wrap around. Otherwise they are the two ends of an open range
/// with only one neighbour each, so a spectrum still rising at an end of the range peaks
/// there. A spectrum that is constant over a grid of two or more points has no peak; a
/// one-point open grid peaks at its only point.
fn find_peaks(scores: &[f64], angles: &[f64], n: usize, circular: bool) -> Vec<f64> {
    let len = scores.len();
    if len == 0 || n == 0 {
        return Vec::new();
    }

    // Runs of equal scores as inclusive index ranges.
    let mut runs: Vec<(usize, usize)> = Vec::new();
    let mut run_start = 0;
    for i in 1..=len {
        if i == len || scores[i] != scores[run_start] {
            runs.push((run_start, i - 1));
            run_start = i;
        }
    }
    if runs.len() == 1 {
        // A single point on an open range has no neighbours, so it is a peak (as for
        // `angle_steps_num = 1`); a longer constant spectrum has none.
        return if len == 1 && !circular {
            vec![angles[0]]
        } else {
            Vec::new()
        };
    }
    // On the circle, a run at the start continues the run at the end. Its indices then
    // go past `len` and are taken modulo `len`.
    if circular && scores[0] == scores[len - 1] {
        let (_, first_end) = runs.remove(0);
        runs.last_mut().unwrap().1 = first_end + len;
    }

    let score = |i: usize| scores[i % len];
    let midpoint = |(a, b): (usize, usize)| {
        if b < len {
            (angles[a] + angles[b]) / 2.0
        } else {
            let step = angles[1] - angles[0];
            let mid = (a + b) as f64 / 2.0;
            if mid >= len as f64 {
                angles[0] + step * (mid - len as f64)
            } else {
                angles[a] + step * (mid - a as f64)
            }
        }
    };

    let r = runs.len();
    let mut peaks: Vec<(f64, f64)> = (0..r)
        .filter_map(|k| {
            let (a, b) = runs[k];
            let prev = match k {
                0 if circular => Some(score(runs[r - 1].1)),
                0 => None,
                _ => Some(score(runs[k - 1].1)),
            };
            let next = match k + 1 {
                j if j < r => Some(score(runs[j].0)),
                _ if circular => Some(score(runs[0].0)),
                _ => None,
            };
            let v = score(a);
            (prev.is_none_or(|p| v > p) && next.is_none_or(|q| v > q))
                .then(|| (v, midpoint((a, b))))
        })
        .collect();

    peaks.sort_unstable_by(|a, b| b.0.total_cmp(&a.0));
    peaks.into_iter().take(n).map(|(_, a)| a).collect()
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Bin selection for IFB-MUSIC
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Picks the STFT bins that carry signal, for [`MusicEstimator::ifb_music_spectrum`].
///
/// IFB-MUSIC weights every bin equally, so bins holding only noise point the merged
/// spectrum in arbitrary directions. This keeps the bins whose power is within
/// `threshold_db` of the strongest bin. A bin's power is the trace of its cross-spectral
/// matrix: `|X|²` summed over microphones and averaged over windows, using the same
/// non-overlapping `nfft`-sample STFT windows as `ifb_music_spectrum`.
///
/// The DC bin is never selected (as with `bins = None`). Returns bin indices in ascending
/// order.
///
/// A tone between two bins leaks into its neighbours, and each selected bin is steered at
/// the bin's frequency rather than the tone's. The mismatch shifts the estimate, most
/// near endfire (0° / 180° for a line array): on the test recordings at `nfft = 1024`
/// (15.6 Hz bins), a single tone is off by up to 5.5° at 0° and 1.5° elsewhere. Choose
/// `nfft` so the tones fall on bins where possible.
///
/// # Errors
/// - [`MusicError::InvalidThreshold`] if `threshold_db` is negative or not finite.
/// - [`MusicError::InvalidNfft`] if `nfft` is 0; [`MusicError::NoUsableBins`] if it is
///   1 (the only bin is DC).
/// - [`MusicError::EmptyData`], [`MusicError::NonFiniteData`] or
///   [`MusicError::DataShorterThanWindow`] for unusable data.
/// - [`MusicError::SilentData`] if every bin except DC has zero power.
///
/// # Examples
/// ```
/// use musicrs::{MusicEstimator, select_bins_by_energy};
/// use nalgebra::DMatrix;
/// use std::f64::consts::PI;
///
/// // A 1 kHz tone: with nfft = 160 at 16 kHz the bins are 100 Hz apart, so it is bin 10.
/// let est = MusicEstimator::default();
/// let data = DMatrix::from_fn(4, 16000, |_, t| (2.0 * PI * 1000.0 * t as f64 / 16000.0).cos());
/// let bins = select_bins_by_energy(&data, 160, 20.0)?;
/// assert_eq!(bins, [10]);
/// let (spectrum, angles) = est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, 160, 1, Some(&bins))?;
/// # let _ = (spectrum, angles);
/// # Ok::<(), musicrs::MusicError>(())
/// ```
pub fn select_bins_by_energy(
    data: &DMatrix<f64>,
    nfft: usize,
    threshold_db: f64,
) -> Result<Vec<usize>> {
    if !(threshold_db.is_finite() && threshold_db >= 0.0) {
        return Err(MusicError::InvalidThreshold(threshold_db));
    }
    if nfft == 0 {
        return Err(MusicError::InvalidNfft);
    }
    if nfft == 1 {
        return Err(MusicError::NoUsableBins);
    }
    check_real_samples(data)?;
    if data.ncols() < nfft {
        return Err(MusicError::DataShorterThanWindow {
            nfft,
            samples: data.ncols(),
        });
    }
    let mut power = vec![0.0; nfft / 2 + 1];
    for m in 0..data.nrows() {
        let row: Vec<f64> = data.row(m).iter().copied().collect();
        for (p, bin) in power.iter_mut().zip(stft(&row, nfft, 0)?) {
            *p += bin.iter().map(|c| c.norm_sqr()).sum::<f64>() / bin.len() as f64;
        }
    }
    let strongest = power[1..].iter().copied().fold(0.0, f64::max);
    if strongest <= 0.0 {
        return Err(MusicError::SilentData);
    }
    let floor = strongest * 10f64.powf(-threshold_db / 10.0);
    Ok((1..power.len()).filter(|&k| power[k] >= floor).collect())
}

/// A power of two close to `max_abs`, the largest absolute value in some data, to divide
/// the data by. MUSIC does not depend on the data's scale, and dividing by a power of two
/// is exact, so this changes no result: it only keeps the sums of squares in the
/// covariance and energy from overflowing for very loud data (or underflowing for very
/// quiet data).
fn power_of_two_scale(max_abs: f64) -> f64 {
    if max_abs > 0.0 {
        2f64.powi((max_abs.log2().floor() as i32).clamp(-1000, 1000))
    } else {
        1.0
    }
}

/// `data` divided by [`power_of_two_scale`] of its largest absolute value.
fn normalised_real(data: &DMatrix<f64>) -> DMatrix<f64> {
    data / power_of_two_scale(data.amax())
}

/// The mean of `values`, summed with Neumaier's compensated summation so that it is
/// correct to about one ulp: subtracting it from constant data then leaves (almost)
/// nothing, which [`SILENCE_RATIO`] relies on. With a plain sum, 16000 samples of 0.3
/// leave a residue above the threshold.
fn accurate_mean<'a>(values: impl ExactSizeIterator<Item = &'a f64>) -> f64 {
    let n = values.len() as f64;
    let (mut sum, mut compensation) = (0.0_f64, 0.0_f64);
    for &x in values {
        let t = sum + x;
        compensation += if sum.abs() >= x.abs() {
            (sum - t) + x
        } else {
            (x - t) + sum
        };
        sum = t;
    }
    (sum + compensation) / n
}

/// Checks that real data has samples and that all of them are finite.
fn check_real_samples(data: &DMatrix<f64>) -> Result<()> {
    if data.is_empty() {
        return Err(MusicError::EmptyData);
    }
    if !data.iter().all(|x| x.is_finite()) {
        return Err(MusicError::NonFiniteData);
    }
    Ok(())
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// MusicEstimator
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Direction-of-Arrival estimator based on the MUSIC algorithm (R. O. Schmidt, 1986).
///
/// The MUSIC algorithm decomposes the sensor-array covariance matrix into signal and
/// noise subspaces.  Angles where the steering vector is orthogonal to the noise
/// subspace produce peaks in the resulting pseudo-spectrum.
///
/// Functions that take data return [`MusicError`] for data they cannot use (wrong row
/// count, no samples, NaN, silence) and for invalid parameters (too many sources, an
/// unusable STFT size or bin list).
///
/// # Examples
/// ```
/// use musicrs::MusicEstimator;
/// let est = MusicEstimator::default(); // Kinect 4-mic array, 720 angle steps, [0, 2π)
/// ```
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct MusicEstimator {
    /// Antenna (microphone) positions as `[x, y]` pairs in metres.
    pub antenna_positions: Vec<[f64; 2]>,
    /// Number of angle steps in the angular search grid.
    pub angle_steps_num: usize,
    /// Angular search range `(start_rad, end_rad)`; the grid includes `start_rad` and
    /// excludes `end_rad`. A range spanning exactly 2π is treated as the full circle (its
    /// ends are adjacent when picking peaks); any other range is open at both ends.
    pub search_interval: (f64, f64),
    /// Sample rate of the input signal in Hz, used to determine the sign convention
    /// for the steering vector (positive exponent for f < sr/2, negative for f ≥ sr/2).
    pub sample_rate: f64,
}

impl Default for MusicEstimator {
    /// Returns an estimator configured for the 4-element Kinect microphone array
    /// with 720 angle steps over the full circle [0, 2π).
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            antenna_positions: DEFAULT_ANTENNA_POSITIONS.to_vec(),
            angle_steps_num: 720,
            search_interval: (0.0, 2.0 * PI),
            sample_rate: 16000.0,
        }
    }
}

impl MusicEstimator {
    /// Creates a new `MusicEstimator`.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `antenna_positions` – Slice of `[x, y]` positions in metres.
    /// * `angle_steps_num`   – Number of discrete angles to evaluate.
    /// * `search_interval`   – `(start_rad, end_rad)` search range.
    /// * `sample_rate`       – Sample rate in Hz (used for aliasing-aware steering).
    ///
    /// The angle grid is not checked here, because the fields are public and can change
    /// later: the methods that search the grid return [`MusicError::InvalidAngleGrid`]
    /// unless `angle_steps_num > 0` and `search_interval` is finite with `start < end`.
    pub fn new(
        antenna_positions: Vec<[f64; 2]>,
        angle_steps_num: usize,
        search_interval: (f64, f64),
        sample_rate: f64,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            antenna_positions,
            angle_steps_num,
            search_interval,
            sample_rate,
        }
    }

    /// Number of antennas in the array.
    #[inline]
    pub fn n_antennas(&self) -> usize {
        self.antenna_positions.len()
    }

    /// Whether [`search_interval`](Self::search_interval) spans exactly the full circle,
    /// so that the first and last grid angles are neighbours.
    fn covers_full_circle(&self) -> bool {
        let (start, end) = self.search_interval;
        ((end - start).abs() - 2.0 * PI).abs() <= 1e-9
    }

    /// The search grid: `angle_steps_num` angles from `start` (included) to `end`
    /// (excluded). pyMUSIC asserts `start < end` in `MUSICEst.__init__`.
    fn angle_grid(&self) -> Result<Vec<f64>> {
        let (start, end) = self.search_interval;
        let steps = self.angle_steps_num;
        if steps == 0 || !(start.is_finite() && end.is_finite() && start < end) {
            return Err(MusicError::InvalidAngleGrid {
                angle_steps_num: steps,
                search_interval: self.search_interval,
            });
        }
        Ok((0..steps)
            .map(|i| start + (end - start) * i as f64 / steps as f64)
            .collect())
    }

    fn check_rows(&self, got: usize) -> Result<()> {
        if got == self.n_antennas() {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(MusicError::RowCountMismatch {
                expected: self.n_antennas(),
                got,
            })
        }
    }

    fn check_sources(&self, n_sources: usize) -> Result<()> {
        if n_sources < self.n_antennas() {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(MusicError::TooManySources {
                n_sources,
                n_antennas: self.n_antennas(),
            })
        }
    }

    // ─── Core algorithm ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    /// Computes the steering vector for a plane wave arriving from `angle` (radians)
    /// at `frequency` (Hz).
    ///
    /// Element *j* is `exp(+i·2π·f·τⱼ)` where `τⱼ = (pⱼ · d̂) / c` is the projection of
    /// antenna *j*'s position onto the arrival direction, divided by the speed of sound. This
    /// matches the non-conjugated [`analytic_signal`] and STFT bins
    /// (pyMUSIC conjugates its analytic signal and uses `exp(−i·2π·f·τⱼ)`; the two agree below
    /// Nyquist). Relative to [`sample_rate`](Self::sample_rate):
    /// * above Nyquist the exponent is negated, `exp(−i·2π·f·τⱼ)`, because the recorded tone
    ///   is aliased and its phase is conjugated;
    /// * within 0.5 Hz of Nyquist the vector is real, `cos(2π·f·τⱼ)`, because the analytic
    ///   signal there is real too.
    ///
    /// # Examples
    /// ```
    /// use musicrs::MusicEstimator;
    /// let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    /// let sv = est.steering_vector(0.0, 300.0);
    /// assert_eq!(sv.len(), 4);
    /// // All elements have unit magnitude
    /// for c in sv.iter() {
    ///     assert!((c.norm() - 1.0).abs() < 1e-12);
    /// }
    /// ```
    pub fn steering_vector(&self, angle: f64, frequency: f64) -> CVec {
        let dir = [angle.cos(), angle.sin()];
        // For f < Nyquist (sr/2): analytic signal has positive phase → use +exponent.
        // For f > Nyquist: signal aliases in the one-sided FFT; dominant eigenvector
        // phase is conjugated → use −exponent.
        // At exactly Nyquist (f == sr/2): analytic signal is real; noise subspace is
        // also real → use cos(phase) as a real steering vector.
        let nyquist = self.sample_rate / 2.0;
        let phase_sign = if frequency > nyquist {
            -1.0_f64
        } else {
            1.0_f64
        };
        let at_nyquist = (frequency - nyquist).abs() < 0.5;
        CVec::from_iterator(
            self.n_antennas(),
            self.antenna_positions.iter().map(|p| {
                let delay = (p[0] * dir[0] + p[1] * dir[1]) / SPEED_OF_SOUND;
                let phase = phase_sign * 2.0 * PI * frequency * delay;
                if at_nyquist {
                    // Real steering vector: imaginary part is zero
                    Cplx::new(phase.cos(), 0.0)
                } else {
                    Cplx::from_polar(1.0, phase)
                }
            }),
        )
    }

    /// Extracts the noise subspace from the Hermitian covariance matrix `cov`.
    ///
    /// Eigendecomposes `cov`, sorts eigenvectors by ascending eigenvalue magnitude,
    /// and returns the `n − n_sources` columns spanning the noise subspace.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `cov`       – Hermitian covariance matrix (n_antennas × n_antennas).
    /// * `n_sources` – Number of signal sources (must be < n_antennas).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`MusicError::CovarianceShape`] if `cov` is not n_antennas × n_antennas,
    /// [`MusicError::NonFiniteData`] if it contains NaN or infinity, and
    /// [`MusicError::TooManySources`] if `n_sources >= n_antennas`.
    pub fn noise_subspace(&self, cov: &CMatrix, n_sources: usize) -> Result<CMatrix> {
        let n = self.n_antennas();
        if cov.shape() != (n, n) {
            return Err(MusicError::CovarianceShape {
                n_antennas: n,
                rows: cov.nrows(),
                cols: cov.ncols(),
            });
        }
        self.check_sources(n_sources)?;
        if !cov.iter().all(|c| c.re.is_finite() && c.im.is_finite()) {
            return Err(MusicError::NonFiniteData);
        }

        // Eigenvectors in ascending eigenvalue order; the first n_noise columns are the
        // noise subspace (smallest eigenvalues).
        let (_eigenvalues, eigenvectors) = hermitian_eigen(cov);
        let n_noise = cov.nrows() - n_sources;
        Ok(eigenvectors.columns(0, n_noise).into())
    }

    /// Generates the MUSIC pseudo-spectrum.
    ///
    /// For each angle θ in the search grid, the score is `1 / ‖Eₙᴴ · a(θ)‖²`.
    /// High values indicate signal directions of arrival.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `noise_mat` – Noise subspace matrix (n_antennas × n_noise) from
    ///   [`noise_subspace`](Self::noise_subspace).

    /// * `nfft`          – STFT window size.
    /// * `n_sources`     – Number of sources.

    ///   Bins at or above `nfft / 2 + 1` are ignored, and so are bins with no power.

    /// Bin frequencies are derived from [`MusicEstimator::sample_rate`], the same rate
    /// [`steering_vector`](Self::steering_vector) uses for its Nyquist handling.

    /// steered at its aliased frequency and its DOA cannot be recovered here.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// `(spectrum, angles)` — the IFB-MUSIC spectrum and corresponding angles.

    /// # Errors
    /// - [`MusicError::RowCountMismatch`], [`MusicError::EmptyData`],

    ///   [`MusicError::DataShorterThanWindow`] if it has no complete STFT window.

    /// - [`MusicError::SilentData`] if no usable bin has power.
    /// - [`MusicError::InvalidAngleGrid`] if the angle grid is unusable (see [`new`](Self::new)).
    pub fn ifb_music_spectrum(
        &self,
        data: &DMatrix<f64>,
        nfft: usize,
        n_sources: usize,
        bins: Option<&[usize]>,
    ) -> Result<(Vec<f64>, Vec<f64>)> {
        self.check_rows(data.nrows())?;
        check_real_samples(data)?;
        self.check_sources(n_sources)?;

            return Err(MusicError::InvalidNfft);
        }
        if data.ncols() < nfft {
            return Err(MusicError::DataShorterThanWindow {
                nfft,
                samples: data.ncols(),
            });
        }
        let data = &normalised_real(data);
        let n_mics = data.nrows();
        let freq_bins = nfft / 2 + 1;

        let default_bins: Vec<usize> = (1..freq_bins).collect();
        let active_bins: Vec<usize> = bins
            .unwrap_or(&default_bins)
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|&bin| bin < freq_bins)
            .collect();
        if active_bins.is_empty() {
            return Err(MusicError::NoUsableBins);
        }

        let stfts: Vec<Vec<Vec<Cplx>>> = (0..n_mics)
            .map(|m| {
                let row: Vec<f64> = data.row(m).iter().copied().collect();
                stft(&row, nfft, 0)
            })
            .collect::<Result<_>>()?;
        let n_windows = stfts[0][0].len();

        // Geometric mean, accumulated as a sum of logarithms: the product of hundreds of
        // per-bin spectra overflows f64.
        let mut log_sum: Option<Vec<f64>> = None;
        let mut angles_out: Vec<f64> = Vec::new();
        let mut n_processed = 0usize;

        // Cross-spectral matrix of each bin, averaged over time windows
        let covs: Vec<(usize, CMatrix)> = active_bins
            .into_iter()
            .map(|bin| {
                let bin_slices: Vec<&[Cplx]> = stfts.iter().map(|s| s[bin].as_slice()).collect();
                let mut cov = CMatrix::zeros(n_mics, n_mics);
                for col in (0..n_windows)
                    .map(|w| CVec::from_iterator(n_mics, bin_slices.iter().map(|s| s[w])))
                {
                    cov += &col * col.adjoint();
                }
                (bin, cov.scale(1.0 / n_windows as f64))
            })
            .collect();
        // Silence is judged against the strongest bin of the whole spectrum, DC included,
        // so that a requested bin holding only rounding residue is still recognised.
        let strongest = stfts
            .iter()
            .fold(vec![0.0; freq_bins], |mut power, mic| {
                for (p, bin) in power.iter_mut().zip(mic) {
                    *p += bin.iter().map(|c| c.norm_sqr()).sum::<f64>() / n_windows as f64;
                }
                power
            })
            .into_iter()
            .fold(0.0, f64::max);

        for (bin, cov) in covs {
            if cov.trace().re <= SILENCE_RATIO * strongest {
                // No power in this bin: its noise subspace would be arbitrary.
                continue;
            }
            let frequency = bin as f64 * self.sample_rate / nfft as f64;
            let noise_mat = self.noise_subspace(&cov, n_sources)?;
            let (spec, angles) = self.spectrum(&noise_mat, frequency)?;

            match &mut log_sum {
                None => {
                    log_sum = Some(spec.iter().map(|s| s.ln()).collect());
                    angles_out = angles;
                }
                Some(sum) => {
                    for (acc, s) in sum.iter_mut().zip(spec.iter()) {
                        *acc += s.ln();
                    }
                }
            }
            n_processed += 1;
        }

        let sum = log_sum.ok_or(MusicError::SilentData)?;
        let merged: Vec<f64> = sum
            .iter()
            .map(|&v| (v / n_processed as f64).exp())
            .collect();
        Ok((merged, angles_out))
    }

//! Times musicrs on the workloads of `bench/bench_pymusic.py` and writes every sample to a CSV.
//!
//! ```sh
//! cargo run --release --example bench_pymusic -- bench/results/musicrs.csv
//! ```
//!
//! Each workload runs a few warm-up calls, then times every call separately, so the analysis
//! (`bench/analyze.py`) can look at the whole distribution rather than one aggregate. The
//! workloads, recordings and CSV format mirror the Python script; see `bench/README.md`.
//! Set `BENCH_SCALE` (e.g. `0.1`) to scale every sample count for a quick run.

use std::fs::File;
use std::hint::black_box;
use std::io::{BufWriter, Write};
use std::time::Instant;

use musicrs::MusicEstimator;
use nalgebra::DMatrix;

const DATA_DIR: &str = "tests/data/single-source";
const NFFT: usize = 160;
const FREQ: u32 = 1400;
const WARMUP: usize = 3;

/// A 4-channel, 24-bit PCM WAV file as a `(4 × n)` matrix normalised by 2²³ (as the tests).
fn read_wav_4ch(path: &str) -> DMatrix<f64> {
    let mut reader = hound::WavReader::open(path).expect("failed to open WAV file");
    let spec = reader.spec();
    assert_eq!((spec.channels, spec.bits_per_sample), (4, 24));
    let raw: Vec<i32> = reader.samples::<i32>().map(Result::unwrap).collect();
    let scale = 2.0_f64.powi(23);
    DMatrix::from_fn(4, raw.len() / 4, |ch, t| raw[t * 4 + ch] as f64 / scale)
}

type Workload = Box<dyn Fn(&MusicEstimator, &DMatrix<f64>)>;

fn main() {
    let out_path = std::env::args()
        .nth(1)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "bench/results/musicrs.csv".into());
    let scale: f64 = std::env::var("BENCH_SCALE").map_or(1.0, |s| s.parse().expect("BENCH_SCALE"));

    let one_bin = [FREQ as usize * NFFT / 16000];
    let all_bins: Vec<usize> = (1..=NFFT / 2).collect();
    // (workload, call, recordings, samples per recording). Same calls and recordings as
    // bench_pymusic.py; musicrs is fast enough for many more samples.
    let workloads: Vec<(&str, Workload, &[&str], usize)> = vec![
        (
            "narrowband",
            Box::new(|est, d| {
                black_box(est.estimate_doa_from_real(d, 1, FREQ as f64).unwrap());
            }),
            &["1.0", "2.0"],
            1000,
        ),
        (
            "ifb_one_bin",
            Box::new(move |est, d| {
                black_box(est.ifb_music_spectrum(d, NFFT, 1, Some(&one_bin)).unwrap());
            }),
            &["1.0", "2.0"],
            1000,
        ),
        (
            "ifb_all_bins",
            Box::new(move |est, d| {
                black_box(est.ifb_music_spectrum(d, NFFT, 1, Some(&all_bins)).unwrap());
            }),
            &["1.0"],
            1000,
        ),
    ];

    if let Some(dir) = std::path::Path::new(&out_path).parent() {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir).expect("create output directory");
    }
    let mut out = BufWriter::new(File::create(&out_path).expect("create output CSV"));
    writeln!(out, "implementation,workload,recording_s,iteration,seconds").unwrap();

    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    for (name, run, durations, samples) in &workloads {
        for duration in *durations {
            let data = read_wav_4ch(&format!(
                "{DATA_DIR}/single-source_{FREQ}Hz_40deg_{duration}s.wav"
            ));
            let samples = ((*samples as f64 * scale).round() as usize).max(5);
            for _ in 0..WARMUP {
                run(&est, black_box(&data));
            }
            for i in 0..samples {
                let t0 = Instant::now();
                run(&est, black_box(&data));
                let dt = t0.elapsed().as_secs_f64();
                writeln!(out, "musicrs,{name},{duration},{i},{dt:e}").unwrap();
            }
            eprintln!("musicrs {name} {duration}s: {samples} samples");
        }
    }
    out.flush().unwrap();

I reviewed all of `HEAD` (b5552e5) plus your uncommitted edits, and ran edge-case checks against the current tree from a throwaway crate (`/tmp/claude-1000/-home-orchid-projects-musicrs/860b07ee-3f92-4815-ab52-690d0ae10c8e/scratchpad/probe`). I didn't run `cargo test` on your in-progress diff.

**Overall:** the attack surface is small. There's no `unsafe` anywhere in `src/`, and the library does no I/O or file parsing (WAV reading is only in tests). Data validation is careful: it checks for NaN/inf, silence, row counts and source counts, and scales loud or quiet input by a power of two. The realistic security risk is denial of service from caller-controlled sizes. Beyond that there's one real correctness bug and some CI hardening.

## Your uncommitted diff

It already covers what I would have flagged next: unchecked `frequency`, `sample_rate` and antenna positions, search spans wider than 2π, and requested bin 0. Before your change, `estimate_doa_from_real(.., frequency = NaN)` quietly returned `Ok([])`. Your new checks look right. `ifb_music_spectrum` doesn't need `check_frequency`, because bins are now forced into `1..=nfft/2`, so every bin frequency is positive.

## Findings, most important first

**1. `select_bins_by_energy` gives wrong answers for very loud or very quiet data** (`src/music.rs`, `select_bins_by_energy`)
It is the only data entry point that doesn't call `normalised_real`, so its FFT power sums overflow or underflow. With one 1 kHz tone scaled by different factors:

| scale | `select_bins_by_energy` | `ifb_music_spectrum` / narrowband |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 bin ✔ | ok |
| 1e‑170 | `Err(SilentData)` ✘ | ok |
| 1e300 | 80 bins (every bin) ✘ | ok |

The fix is one line: run `normalised_real(data)` after `check_real_samples`, as `ifb_music_spectrum` does.

**2. `stft` can crash the whole process on a huge `nfft` (DoS)** (`src/stft.rs`, `stft`)
It plans the FFT and allocates `nfft/2+1` bins before checking the data length. `stft(&[0.0; 4], 1 << 40, 0)` hits `memory allocation of 3758096384 bytes failed` and exits with code 134. A failed allocation can't be caught, so a caller who passes `nfft` from untrusted config loses the process. That contradicts the "does not panic" promise in CLAUDE.md. Fix it by returning early when `data.len() < nfft`, before planning: either return `DataShorterThanWindow` or build the empty result without a plan. The other entry points already check `ncols >= nfft` first, which bounds their memory by the input size.

**3. A huge `angle_steps_num` panics** (`angle_grid`)
`angle_steps_num = usize::MAX / 2` panics with `capacity overflow`. Since this is a public field, consider an upper limit or `try_reserve` that returns `InvalidAngleGrid`. Otherwise, document that the grid size is the caller's responsibility.

**4. IFB memory grows with the number of microphones** (`ifb_music_spectrum`)
`covs` holds every bin's covariance matrix at once before the silence check runs. That is about `n_mics² × nfft/2 × 16` bytes, so with `nfft ≈ N` memory is roughly `n_mics` times the input size. Building each covariance inside the `for (bin, cov)` loop keeps only one alive at a time, which saves memory and keeps the same results.

**5. Smaller API points**
- Duplicate entries in `bins` are counted more than once in the geometric mean, which quietly weights them. Deduplicate them or document it.
- `n_sources = 0` returns `Ok([])`. Consider an error, or say so in the docs.
- Each call to `analytic_signal` and `stft` creates a new `FftPlanner`, and they run once per channel, so FFT plans are rebuilt every time. This costs speed only, not correctness.

## CI and supply chain (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)
- **Third-party actions are pinned to tags that can move** (`@v4`, `@v2`, `@stable`). `EnricoMi/...`, `taiki-e/...`, `Swatinem/...` and `dtolnay/...` all run with the job's token. Pin them to commit SHAs (Dependabot can keep those up to date).
- **`pull-requests: write` and `checks: write` apply to the whole job**, including `cargo build` and the tests, which run dependency build scripts. Move publishing into its own job, or a `workflow_run` workflow, so only that step gets write access. On fork PRs the token is read-only anyway, so the publish step will fail there.
- No `--locked` on build/test, so Cargo.lock isn't enforced.
- No `cargo audit` or `cargo deny` job. Neither tool is installed here, so I couldn't check dependencies for known advisories.

I re-ran `cargo test` on the current working tree, including your uncommitted edits, and it passed: 105 tests, 0 failures, 9 skipped as slow (`#[ignore = "slow"]`). No other cargo process was running, so the collision that caused the earlier "Permission denied" didn't happen again.

so your vode review just showed nothing?

No. Two different things happened:

- **`/ultrareview` showed nothing.** It only reviews changes against a base branch, and you were on a clean `main` with no commits or edits, so it had nothing to look at. I can't start it myself either.
- **So I reviewed the whole codebase by hand instead.** My earlier reply has the full write-up, from before the test-hook messages. Here are the findings again:

**Bugs (confirmed by running them)**
1. **`select_bins_by_energy` gives wrong answers for very loud or very quiet data.** It's the only entry point that doesn't call `normalised_real`. A tone at 1e‑170 scale returns `Err(SilentData)`, and at 1e300 it picks all 80 bins instead of 1. The fix is one line.
2. **`stft` crashes the process on a huge `nfft`.** `stft(&[0.0; 4], 1 << 40, 0)` makes an allocation that fails and aborts with exit 134, which can't be caught. It plans the FFT before checking the data length. If `nfft` comes from untrusted input, this is a denial-of-service risk.
3. **A huge `angle_steps_num` panics** with "capacity overflow", which goes against the "public API does not panic" rule.

**Smaller issues**
4. `ifb_music_spectrum` holds every bin's covariance matrix at once. Memory grows with mics² × nfft, and building each one inside the loop avoids that.
5. Duplicate entries in `bins` count more than once in the mean. `n_sources = 0` returns `Ok([])`. A new FFT planner is built on every call.

**CI and supply chain**
6. The actions are pinned to tags that can be moved, not to commit SHAs.
7. `pull-requests: write` and `checks: write` apply to the whole job, including build and tests.
8. There's no `--locked`, no `cargo audit` or `cargo deny` step, and no CI run on pushes to `main`.
9. `faer` (0.19, latest 0.24) and `nalgebra` (0.33, latest 0.35) are behind.

**Already handled by your uncommitted edits:** the checks for frequency, sample rate and antenna positions, and the 2π limit on the search span. Before them, a NaN frequency quietly returned `Ok([])`.

Want me to fix 1 and 2 on a `fix/` branch, each with a regression test?
fix all, but not 3. use an agent team and split tasks into branches on your behalf

- `stft` planned the FFT and allocated `nfft/2+1` bins before checking that one window fits, so `stft(&[0.0; 4], 1 << 40, 0)` aborted the process ("memory allocation of 3758096384 bytes failed"), which can'\''t be caught.
- It now returns `MusicError::DataShorterThanWindow` before planning anything, so memory is bounded by the input size. Parameter errors (`InvalidNfft`, `InvalidOverlap`) still come first.
- **Behaviour change:** data shorter than `nfft` used to give `nfft/2+1` empty bins and is now an error. The internal callers already check this first.

## Tests
- `stft_rejects_data_shorter_than_window` (unit test) and `stft_errors` in `tests/errors_test.rs`.

gh pr create --base feat/test-gaps-3 --head 'fix/select-bins-scale' --title 'Normalise the data in select_bins_by_energy' --body '## Summary
- `select_bins_by_energy` was the only data entry point that didn'\''t call `normalised_real`, so its STFT power sums underflowed or overflowed. A 1 kHz tone scaled by 1e-170 gave `Err(SilentData)`, and scaled by 1e300 it selected all 80 bins instead of bin 10.
- It now divides by the same power of two as the other entry points. That division is exact, so results at normal scales don'\''t change.

## Tests
- `select_bins_by_energy_does_not_depend_on_scale` checks scales from 1e-300 to 1e300, a two-tone case, and that DC-only data is still silent.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -- --include-ignored` pass.

name: CI

on:
  # Every pull request, whatever its base, so PRs stacked on another PR's branch get CI too
  pull_request:
  # main itself after merges
  push:
    branches: [main]

# A newer push to the same branch or PR supersedes the run in progress
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# Least privilege: jobs get read-only access unless they ask for more
permissions:
  contents: read

# Third-party actions are pinned to full commit SHAs; Dependabot (.github/dependabot.yml) keeps them current
jobs:
  test:
    name: Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@df2a88e9fe4098bad09cb42c3dec7187f15861fc # master
        with:
          toolchain: stable
          components: rustfmt, clippy

      - name: Cache cargo registry & build artifacts
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@d1527c8f67ef9af357290475d4af4b0fab8f12e0 # v2.9.3

      - name: Install cargo-nextest
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@fe3acb53a98b62c772db35de75ce0e4595e7ca8c # v2.90.8
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest

      - name: Check formatting
        run: cargo fmt --check

      - name: Clippy
        run: cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings

      - name: Build
        run: cargo build --locked --all-targets

      - name: Run tests (nextest + JUnit output)
        run: |
          cargo nextest run \
            --locked \
            --profile ci \
            --run-ignored all \
            --no-fail-fast \
            2>&1

      - name: Upload JUnit XML
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit
          path: target/nextest/ci/junit.xml
          if-no-files-found: warn

  # The only job with write access; it runs no repository code, it only reads the test job's JUnit XML
  publish-test-results:
    name: Publish test results
    needs: test
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      checks: write
      pull-requests: write

    steps:
      - name: Download JUnit XML
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: junit
          path: junit

      - name: Publish test results
        uses: EnricoMi/publish-unit-test-result-action@da5b7be67623cd59bbbd1a0ce4f022050a55605f # v2.26.0
        with:
          files: junit/junit.xml
          check_name: Test Results
          comment_mode: always
          fail_on: test failures

  audit:
    name: Dependency audit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@df2a88e9fe4098bad09cb42c3dec7187f15861fc # master
        with:
          toolchain: stable

      - name: Install cargo-audit
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@fe3acb53a98b62c772db35de75ce0e4595e7ca8c # v2.90.8
        with:
          tool: cargo-audit

      # Checks Cargo.lock against the RustSec advisory database
      - name: Audit dependencies
        run: cargo audit

content.text:
All seven fixes are pushed and open as PRs, each stacked on #21 (`feat/test-gaps-3`). I re-ran every branch in a clean target directory of my own: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo test -- --include-ignored` all pass. GitHub CI has only just started on them.

| PR | Branch | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| [#22](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/musicrs/pull/22) | `fix/stft-huge-nfft` | `stft` returns `DataShorterThanWindow` instead of crashing on a huge `nfft` |
| [#23](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/musicrs/pull/23) | `fix/ifb-memory` | IFB holds one covariance matrix at a time; repeated `bins` count once |
| [#24](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/musicrs/pull/24) | `fix/zero-sources` | New `MusicError::NoSources` for `n_sources = 0` |
| [#25](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/musicrs/pull/25) | `fix/select-bins-scale` | `select_bins_by_energy` picks the same bins from 1e‑300 to 1e300 |
| [#26](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/musicrs/pull/26) | `fix/fft-planner-reuse` | One FFT planner per call instead of one per channel; output unchanged |
| [#27](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/musicrs/pull/27) | `fix/ci-hardening` | Actions pinned to commit SHAs, write access only in the publish job, `--locked`, `cargo audit`, Dependabot, CI on `main` |
| [#28](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/musicrs/pull/28) | `fix/dependency-updates` | `faer` 0.24 and `nalgebra` 0.35 |

**Decisions for you:**
- **#28 needs Rust 1.89.** Your default toolchain is 1.88, and once this merges a plain `cargo test` fails there, so the Stop hook will fail too. Run `rustup update stable` first.
- **#28 regenerates the four `*.narrowband.musicrs.csv` snapshots.** With the new `faer`, the values at the spectrum peaks moved by up to 5e‑8, against a 1e‑9 tolerance. Only those peak values change, where the result depends on rounding. The comparisons against pyMUSIC and scipy are exactly the same as before, and the tolerance itself is unchanged. Snapshot tests at the peaks will likely break again on future solver updates, so it may be worth testing those points differently.
- **#27 turned up a real vulnerability.** `cargo audit` found RUSTSEC-2026-0204 in `crossbeam-epoch` 0.9.18, which comes in through `faer`, and #27 updates it to 0.9.21. #28 already has 0.9.21, so the `Cargo.lock` conflict between them resolves to the same version.

**Things to know:**
- **Not every API change is a new error type.** #24 adds a new error type. #22 changes behaviour: data shorter than the window is now an error instead of returning empty bins.

//   * `*.eigh.csv` – pyMUSIC with `np.linalg.eig` swapped for the Hermitian `eigh`.

//   * `*.eig.csv`  – pyMUSIC as published. On this nearly noiseless data `eig`
//     returns a non-orthogonal noise basis, so the values are basis-dependent; only
//     the peak location is compared.
//   * `*.hilbert_n<N>.scipy.csv` – `scipy.signal.hilbert` of one channel, compared

// At and above Nyquist (8000 Hz and 9100 Hz here) musicrs deliberately differs from
// pyMUSIC (real steering vector at f == sr/2, conjugated one above it; see CLAUDE.md
// "Sign convention"), so there is no pyMUSIC reference. Instead
// `*.narrowband.musicrs.csv` are snapshots of musicrs's OWN output, not pyMUSIC
// references: they pin that behaviour so it cannot change silently. Regenerate them

fn read_golden(name: &str) -> (Vec<f64>, Vec<f64>) {
    let text = fs::read_to_string(Path::new(GOLDEN_DIR).join(name))
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("cannot read golden file {name}: {e}"));
    text.lines()
        .skip(1)
        .map(|line| {
            let (a, s) = line.split_once(',').unwrap();
            (a.parse::<f64>().unwrap(), s.parse::<f64>().unwrap())
        })
        .unzip()
}

fn argmax(v: &[f64]) -> usize {
    (0..v.len()).max_by(|&a, &b| v[a].total_cmp(&v[b])).unwrap()
}

/// Compare a musicrs spectrum against both golden variants of `prefix`.
fn check(prefix: &str, angles: &[f64], spectrum: &[f64]) {
    // Value-by-value against pyMUSIC with a Hermitian eigensolver
    let (g_angles, g_spectrum) = read_golden(&format!("{prefix}.eigh.csv"));
    assert_eq!(angles.len(), g_angles.len(), "{prefix}: grid size differs");
    for (a, g) in angles.iter().zip(&g_angles) {
        assert!(
            (a - g).abs() < 1e-9,
            "{prefix}: angle grid differs ({a} vs {g})"
        );
    }
    let err = spectrum
        .iter()
        .zip(&g_spectrum)
        .map(|(s, g)| (s - g).abs() / g.abs())
        .fold(0.0, f64::max);
    println!("{prefix}: max relative error vs eigh {err:.3e}");
    assert!(
        err < REL_TOLERANCE,
        "{prefix}: deviates from pyMUSIC (eigh) by {err:.3e}"
    );

    // Peak location against pyMUSIC as published (within one grid step, circularly). The
    // line array's spectrum has equal peaks at θ and 360° − θ (grid index n − i), and
    // rounding decides which one is the argmax, so either counts.
    let (_, orig) = read_golden(&format!("{prefix}.eig.csv"));
    let (ours, theirs) = (argmax(spectrum), argmax(&orig));
    let n = spectrum.len();
    let circular_steps = |a: usize, b: usize| {
        let d = (a + n - b) % n;
        d.min(n - d)
    };
    let steps = circular_steps(ours, theirs).min(circular_steps(ours, (n - theirs) % n));
    println!(
        "{prefix}: peak {:.1}° vs pyMUSIC (eig) {:.1}°",
        angles[ours].to_degrees(),
        angles[theirs].to_degrees()
    );
    assert!(
        steps <= 1,
        "{prefix}: peak differs from pyMUSIC (eig) by {steps} grid steps"
    );
}

const SNAPSHOT_CASES: [(&str, f64); 4] = [

    ("single-source_9100Hz_80deg_1.0s", 9100.0),

/// Snapshots compare musicrs with itself, so only floating-point noise across

fn narrowband_spectrum_matches_musicrs_snapshot_at_and_above_nyquist() {
    let update = std::env::var("MUSICRS_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS").is_ok_and(|v| v == "1");
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();

        let (spectrum, angles) = narrowband_spectrum(&est, stem, freq);
        let name = format!("{stem}.narrowband.musicrs.csv");
        if update {
            let mut csv = String::from("angle_rad,spectrum\n");
            for (a, s) in angles.iter().zip(&spectrum) {
                csv.push_str(&format!("{a:?},{s:?}\n"));
            }
            fs::write(Path::new(GOLDEN_DIR).join(&name), csv).unwrap();
            println!("{name}: snapshot rewritten");
            continue;
        }
        let (s_angles, s_spectrum) = read_golden(&name);
        assert_eq!(angles, s_angles, "{name}: angle grid differs");
        let err = spectrum
            .iter()
            .zip(&s_spectrum)
            .map(|(s, g)| (s - g).abs() / g.abs())
            .fold(0.0, f64::max);
        println!("{name}: max relative error vs snapshot {err:.3e}");
        assert!(
            err < SNAPSHOT_REL_TOLERANCE,
            "{name}: musicrs output changed by {err:.3e} relative to its snapshot; if \

        );
    }
}

content.text:
I fixed the snapshot test: it no longer fails on rounding noise at the peaks, and it still catches real changes in behaviour. It's committed on a new branch, `fix/snapshot-peak-tolerance` (`78342f3`, based on `main`), but not pushed yet.

**What changed** (`tests/golden_test.rs`):
- **What's compared:** instead of each spectrum value's own relative error, the test compares `1 / spectrum`, the MUSIC denominator, scaled by its largest value over the grid.
  - At a peak the denominator is tiny, about the size of rounding error. That's why the old relative check blew up there whenever the eigensolver rounded slightly differently.
